transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because... I just keep getting stuck on this sagging, uneven look around my jaw and on one side of my face. I saw some recent family photos and it really stood out to me, and now I just can't stop focusing on it. My wife says she barely notices anything, and my clients at work don't seem to see it either, but... yeah, it's just really bothering me, so I figured I should talk to someone about it.
About how much time each day would you say you spend thinking about or checking on this asymmetry in your face—like looking in mirrors, taking photos, or trying to hide it?

It's hard to put an exact number on the time, but it definitely adds up throughout the day. It really flares up around work. Like, right before client meetings, I’ll go check the bathroom mirror, or I'll pull up my phone camera several times just to see how bad it looks. I end up trying to adjust the lighting in my office, or maybe I'll mess with my shirt collar and try to sit so my face is angled a certain way. 

And then... well, I also catch myself comparing my face to other people. Like the younger advisors at the firm, or guys I see when my wife and I go out to gallery events. I'll suddenly realize I'm doing that in my head instead of actually focusing on the conversation I'm supposed to be having.

When your wife or others tell you they don't notice any asymmetry, do you think it's possible they're right and you might be overestimating how noticeable it is, or do you feel certain that the flaw is really there regardless of what they say?

I mean, I hear what she's saying, and part of me knows she wouldn't lie to me. But... it's just really hard to believe her. When I look in the mirror or see those photos, it's right there. It's so obvious to me. So, even though she says she doesn't see it, I just feel like maybe she's trying to make me feel better, or maybe people are just being polite. Deep down, I still feel pretty certain it's there and that it looks bad.

Even if only for a brief moment, have you ever been able to seriously consider that this asymmetry might not be as noticeable as you believe, or does it feel like an absolute fact with no room for doubt?

I guess... I'm not entirely sure. I mean, there are times when I think, okay, maybe it's not as bad as I think it is. Like when my wife is so sure she doesn't see anything, I do pause for a second and wonder if I'm just making a mountain out of a molehill. 

So, no, I wouldn't say it's an absolute fact with zero room for doubt. But... even if I can consider that for a minute, it just doesn't really last. As soon as I catch my reflection again or see another picture, the doubt goes away and it's right back to looking obvious to me.
How long have you been preoccupied with this facial asymmetry—did it start recently after seeing those photos, or has it been something you've noticed and worried about for months or longer?

I'm not entirely sure exactly when it started, to be honest. I mean, I guess I've always been a little self-conscious, but... I don't really know if it's been months or if it just kind of crept up on me recently. I just know it's really bothering me now.
Thinking back, can you recall roughly how many weeks or months ago you first started noticing and worrying about this asymmetry, even before it became this intense?

I really can't put a timeline on it. Like I said, I'm just not sure. I don't know if it was a few weeks ago or a few months ago when I first noticed it. I just know it's something I'm dealing with right now, and it's hard to look past it. I can't give you an exact number of weeks or months.
Has this preoccupation with your facial asymmetry caused any real problems for you—for example, avoiding certain meetings, social events, or activities because of how you think you look?

Well, I still get through my work, for the most part. I'm a financial advisor, so I have to see clients. But... I've definitely been slower getting out the door for those meetings lately. It just takes me longer to get ready, trying to make sure I look okay. And during some of the appointments, I'm just less present, you know? I'm distracted by it. 

Outside of work, yeah, it's caused some issues. My wife and I usually go to a lot of art openings, but I've skipped a few of them recently. I just didn't want to be seen by all those people... or worse, photographed. So, it is getting in the way of some things.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient exhibits a preoccupation with a perceived defect in appearance (facial asymmetry) that is not observable or appears slight to others (wife and clients do not notice it). He engages in repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, camera checking, comparing his appearance to others, camouflaging with lighting/collar adjustments) in response to the appearance concerns. This preoccupation causes clinically significant distress and functional impairment (avoiding social/art events, delayed preparation for work, reduced presence during client meetings). Insight is poor but not absent—he can briefly entertain that his wife might be right and the flaw may not be as noticeable, though this doubt is fleeting and he returns to conviction upon checking mirrors/photos. This pattern of insight (poor insight, not delusional) supports classification of Body Dysmorphic Disorder with poor insight rather than a delusional disorder (F22) or OCD (F42.2), where the content of intrusive thoughts is not specifically appearance-based.
